public_rationale: Both parts hold under a plain reading. OpenAI, the largest model maker, expected to lose about $5 billion in 2024 (e4). Fortune reported that the leading model makers were not yet profitable (e5). At least three 2024 license-and-hire deals left investors with little gain. Inflection's investors got a modest return (e1). Adept's investors roughly got their money back (e2). Covariant's investors reportedly got very little (e3). The main counterpoint is Character.AI: its investors were bought out at 2.5 times the last valuation (e6). That is a real profit, though below the $5 billion valuation once discussed. If Marcus meant Character.AI as one of his three, that part is weaker. Even so, three qualifying deals still exist.
limitations: 'Most companies' is not measured directly; the evidence covers the largest firms.
Deal terms come from press reports citing anonymous sources.
Covariant is a robotics-AI company and may not be one of the three Marcus meant.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Most AI model companies have lost money, and at least three have been quasi-acquired with little profit for investors.

statement.excerpt: Most companies involved have thus far lost money. At least three have been quasi-acquired with relatively little profit for their investors.
statement.document_title: 25 AI Predictions for 2025, from Marcus on AI

from_speaker: Most companies involved have thus far lost money
At least three have been quasi-acquired
with relatively little profit for their investors
our_interpretation: 'Companies involved' read as the AI model makers (LLM startups such as OpenAI, Inflection, Adept, Character.AI), excluding chip makers like Nvidia, which the post sets apart.
'Quasi-acquired' read as the 2024 license-and-hire deals, where a Big Tech firm hired the founders and staff and paid a license fee without buying the company.
'Relatively little profit for their investors' read as investors getting back roughly their money or a modest multiple, well below the valuations once hoped for.
Period: calendar 2024, up to the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Reports show the leading AI model companies were losing money in 2024, and at least three 2024 quasi-acquisitions returned investors roughly their money or a modest gain.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reports show most AI model companies were profitable, or fewer than three such deals happened, or the deals gave investors large returns.

evidence.excerpt: The deal will make Inflection’s investors whole, as Bloomberg previously reported, with a modest return on investment.
evidence.explanation: Inflection was quasi-acquired by Microsoft and its investors got only a modest return. This fits 'relatively little profit'.

evidence.excerpt: investors like Greylock and General Catalyst, who put $414 million into the company, will roughly recoup their investment.
evidence.explanation: Adept's investors roughly got their money back after Amazon hired its staff. That is a second quasi-acquisition with little or no profit.

evidence.excerpt: Covariant's founders received substantial payouts while investors and rank-and-file employees had their equity stakes substantially diluted and received very little.
evidence.locator: section 2024 Amazon Agreement and Zombie Company status
evidence.explanation: Amazon's August 2024 license-and-hire deal with Covariant reportedly left investors with very little. That would be a third such deal.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT, expects about $5 billion in losses on $3.7 billion in revenue this year, CNBC has confirmed.
evidence.explanation: The largest AI model company expected to lose about $5 billion in 2024. This supports the 'lost money' part.

evidence.excerpt: While they may have the strongest chance of eventually achieving profitability, there are still questions as to whether foundation model companies can ever make money.
evidence.explanation: A contemporaneous report describes the leading model makers as not yet profitable. This supports the general 'lost money' statement.

evidence.excerpt: the deal involves a buyout of existing investors’ shares at a valuation of $2.5 billion, a marked increase from its previous valuation of $1 billion.
evidence.explanation: Character.AI investors were bought out at 2.5 times the last valuation. That is a real profit, so this deal does not clearly fit 'relatively little profit', though it was below the $5 billion once discussed.
